terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js starts your API on a free port and sends it a few requests, some with the staff key.

tasks.title: Move the routes into a router
tasks.description:
Implement `workshopsRouter(store)` in `src/routes/workshops.js`. It returns an Express router with all six workshop routes from `src/app.js`: list (with its filters), read one, create, replace, change and remove. Every answer stays exactly as it is now.

- the router's paths are written from where it is mounted: the list is at `/`, one workshop at `/:id`
- in `createApp`, remove those routes and mount the router at `/workshops`; `GET /health` and the catch-all 404 stay in `app.js`
- the `location` of a new workshop still names its real path, such as `/workshops/6`

The check mounts your router at a different path in an app of its own and sends it every kind of request, then checks that `createApp` still answers at `/workshops`.
nextSteps: Make a router in `workshopsRouter` and return it.
Move each workshop route onto it, and shorten its path.
Move the helpers the routes need with them.
Mount the router in `createApp`, then run `node try.js`.
hints: A router is a small app with routes and middleware of its own. It has the same `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete` methods.
`express.Router()` makes one, and `app.use('/workshops', router)` mounts it. Inside, the router only sees the part of the path after `/workshops`. `req.baseUrl` holds the part before.
`router.get('/:id', ...)` instead of `app.get('/workshops/:id', ...)`, and `res.location(`${req.baseUrl}/${workshop.id}`)` for the new workshop.

tasks.title: Let only staff make changes
tasks.description:
Implement `staffOnly(key)` in `src/middleware/staffOnly.js`. It returns a middleware:

- `GET` and `HEAD` requests go on to the next handler
- any other request goes on only when its `x-staff-key` header equals `key`
- otherwise it answers `401` with `{ "error": { "code": "unauthorized", "message": "..." } }` and the route never runs

Then use it in `createApp`: put `staffOnly(staffKey)` in front of the workshops router, with the `staffKey` that `createApp` is given.

The check starts your app with a key of its own and sends reads and changes with no key, a wrong key and the right one.
nextSteps: Return a function with the three middleware arguments from `staffOnly`.
Compare the header with the key, and either go on or answer 401.
Mount it in front of the router, then run `node try.js`.
hints: A middleware ends in one of two ways: it answers, or it calls `next()` so the next handler runs. Never both.
`req.get('x-staff-key')` reads a header, whatever case the client wrote it in. `app.use(path, first, second)` runs both handlers in order on that path.

`return (req, res, next) => { ... }` with `return next()` for reads and for the right key, and `res.status(401).json(...)` for the rest. Mount it as `app.use('/workshops', staffOnly(staffKey), workshopsRouter(store))`.

tasks.title: Answer every error as JSON
tasks.description:
Implement `handleErrors(err, req, res, next)` in `src/middleware/errors.js`, the app's one error handler:

- a body that is not valid JSON answers `400` with `{ "error": { "code": "invalid_json", "message": "..." } }`
- any other error is logged with `console.error` and answers `500` with `{ "error": { "code": "internal", "message": "..." } }`; the message says nothing about the error itself: no stack, no error message, no file paths
- if the response has already started, pass the error on with `next(err)`

Register it in `createApp` after everything else. The check makes the store fail with an error of its own, posts broken JSON, and checks that ordinary requests and the 404 still work.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js` and read what broken JSON gets today.
Tell a JSON error from everything else.
Log the error for yourself and send a plain sentence to the client.
Register the handler last in `createApp`, then run `node try.js` again.
hints: Express knows a function is an error handler because it takes four arguments. It only runs once something has failed.
The error `express.json()` passes on for a broken body has a `type` of `'entity.parse.failed'` and a `status` of 400.

`if (res.headersSent) return next(err)`, then `if (err.type === 'entity.parse.failed') return res.status(400).json(...)`, then `console.error(err)` and `res.status(500).json(...)`. Add it with `app.use(handleErrors)` after the catch-all.
